related_questions.question: Who gets COVID rebound after Paxlovid?
related_questions.snippet: Pfizer research showed a rebound in 2.3% of participants who took Paxlovid and 1.7% in the control group (where participants didn't get the pill). In a different study, 14% of those who took Paxlovid experienced a rebound, and so did 9% of those who didn't get Paxlovid.
related_questions.title: What Is Paxlovid Rebound? 9 Things to Know > News > Yale Medicine

related_questions.question: Are you still contagious with COVID if you're taking Paxlovid?
related_questions.snippet: You can still spread the virus while taking Paxlovid, and how long you are contagious depends on many factors. In addition to possibly making you less contagious, Paxlovid has been shown to lower the risk of hospitalization from COVID-19 infection by over 50% and the risk of death by 75%.
related_questions.title: Does Paxlovid make you less contagious? - Drugs.com

related_questions.question: Do all COVID patients get Paxlovid?
related_questions.snippet: Paxlovid is available to anyone ages 12 and up, depending on their risk for severe illness from COVID. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) gave the drug full approval in May 2023 for adults with mild-to-moderate COVID at high risk for severe disease, hospitalization, and death.

related_questions.question: Is it safe to travel to the Czech Republic now?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, it is generally safe to travel to the Czech Republic. The country is considered one of the safest in Europe, with a low crime rate, especially in major cities like Prague. However, as with any popular tourist destination, petty crime like pickpocketing and scams can occur, particularly in crowded areas.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, it is generally safe to travel to the Czech Republic

list.title: Overall Safety:
list.snippet: The Czech Republic ranks high in global safety indices, with a low crime rate and a strong police presence.

list.title: Petty Crime:
list.snippet: Be aware of your surroundings, especially in crowded tourist areas like Prague's Old Town Square or Charles Bridge.

list.title: Scams:
list.snippet: Be cautious of tourist scams, such as overcharging by taxi drivers or currency exchange scams.

list.title: Public Transportation:
list.snippet: Use official transportation options like licensed taxis or ride-sharing apps to avoid potential issues.

list.title: Night Safety:
list.snippet: While cities are generally safe, it's advisable to avoid poorly lit or secluded areas at night, especially when traveling alone.

list.title: Emergency Services:
list.snippet: The Czech Republic has a well-functioning emergency system. In case of an emergency, you can call 112 for assistance.

list.title: COVID-19:
list.snippet: As of April 9, 2022, there are no COVID-19 related entry restrictions for travelers.
